name: FLORES-101
description: FLORES-101 is an evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains. These sentences have been translated into 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process. The dataset enables assessment of model quality on low-resource languages and evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems, as all translations are multilingually aligned.
creator: Facebook AI Research
inLanguage: 101 languages including English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Arabic, Hindi, and 95 others
citeAs: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan. The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv:2106.03193v1 [cs.CL] 6 Jun 2021
rai:dataCollection: All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources (Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage). A third of the sentences were collected from Wikinews (international news articles), a third from Wikijunior (age-appropriate nonfiction books for children), and a third from WikiVoyage (travel guide with articles about travel tips, food and destinations). The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. One paragraph per document was selected from either the beginning, middle or end of the article, with balanced location selection equally distributed across the whole corpus.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia articles from Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The selection process was performed by 10 different annotators (6 male and 4 female) with different roles in research (researchers, scientists, engineers, program/project managers) originally coming from different regions of the world (East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America). For each sentence, Wikipedia URL, topic, and boolean flags were extracted to indicate whether the sentence contained entities linked to other Wikipedia pages and images. All sentences were manually labeled by a more detailed sub-topic (one of 10 possibilities: crime, disasters, entertainment, geography, health, nature, politics, science, sports, and travel).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were translated by professional translators through Language Service Providers (LSPs). The translation workflow included: (1) translation by an initial LSP, (2) editing within the LSP, (3) automated quality control checks, (4) quality assurance by an independent LSP, and (5) potential re-translation if quality was insufficient. Translations were evaluated based on a Translation Quality Score (0-100 scale) determined by the number of identified errors including grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register. Each error was associated with a severity level (minor, major, or critical). The acceptable translation quality score threshold was set to 90%.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Based on pilot experiments, two translation LSPs were selected that produced the highest quality translations. The workflow A-C-A was chosen where the same LSP handles both translation and re-translation for a given language, with each translation LSP handling half of the languages. Human assessment of translation quality was used to evaluate all translations. If the translation quality score was below the accepted threshold, translations together with the assessment report were sent back to the translation LSP for re-translation. If the initial score was below a certain threshold associated with good translation quality, the re-translated translations were evaluated by humans one more time.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into three splits: dev, devtest, and test. The dev set is meant to be used for hyper-parameter tuning. The devtest is meant to be used for testing purposes during the development phase. The test set will not be released, but will be available via a publicly available evaluation server. The dev and devtest are publicly downloadable.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables better assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages, including the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems. The majority of the world's population speak low-resource languages and would benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages. The dataset supports evaluation of traditionally neglected regionally-relevant language pairs such as Xhosa-Zulu, Vietnamese-Thai, and Spanish-Aymara.
rai:dataBiases: While translationese (overly literal or awkward translations) has known idiosyncrasies, the authors conjecture that these effects are rather marginal when evaluating models in low-resource languages, where current MT systems produce many severe mistakes. All source sentences are from English Wikipedia, which means translations not in English are produced by human translators rather than being naturally occurring text in those languages.
rai:dataLimitations: The only caveat for many-to-many evaluation is that source sentences not in English are produced by human translators. The dataset focuses on evaluation rather than training. Performance is heavily correlated with amount of training data available for each language. Translation between very low-resource and low-resource languages yields very low spBLEU scores (less than 5), indicating that lack of training data strongly limits performance of current MT systems.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluation of machine translation systems, particularly for low-resource languages and many-to-many multilingual translation. It supports evaluation of document-level translation and multimodal translation. The dataset can also be used to evaluate tasks such as sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation. The dataset is meant to foster progress in the machine translation community and beyond.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each sentence has one translation per target language (101 languages total). For quality assurance, translations were evaluated by independent human evaluators from a separate LSP.
rai:annotatorDemographics: The sentence selection process was performed by 10 different annotators: 6 male and 4 female, with different roles in research (researchers, scientists, engineers, program/project managers), originally coming from different regions of the world (East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America). Professional translators were used through Language Service Providers for the actual translation work.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic checks were implemented including: (i) language identification, (ii) checking whether the translation is a copy of the source sentence, (iii) checking whether the translation has significantly different length, (iv) checking translation fluency according to a language model, (v) checking whether the translation is a copy of the translation produced by publicly available translation engines. A heuristic based on sentence-level SentencePiece BLEU was used to detect and reject professional translations that are likely copies from translation engines.
